mechanisms.name: Prime-field trace-one construction
mechanisms.construction: Choose a prime p and a nonsingular curve E/F_p; use a trace-prescribed construction or bounded coefficient search, then certify #E(F_p)=p (t=1). Retain its exact Weierstrass model and point-count certificate.
mechanisms.recognition: Exact trace t=1 over F_p, with a nonzero discriminant.
mechanisms.witness_requirements: Certified field, model, order, selected generator and the hypotheses for the published p-adic reduction.
mechanisms.selected_subgroup_gate: The selected group must be the characteristic-order group covered by the reduction.

mechanisms.name: Factored selected subgroup
mechanisms.construction: Fix a finite field and a chosen factor bound B; enumerate certified curve orders or use trace-prescribed construction until a selected cyclic subgroup has completely factored order r with each prime factor at most B.
mechanisms.recognition: Verify generator order r and a complete certified factorization of r; record B and the sampling law.
mechanisms.witness_requirements: Exact curve, generator, subgroup order, factorization, and component CRT maps.
mechanisms.selected_subgroup_gate: The target point must lie in the certified cyclic group; an ambient-order factorization alone is insufficient.

mechanisms.name: Low embedding-degree selected subgroup
mechanisms.construction: Choose Q, a prime r distinct from char(F_Q), and k with r dividing Q+1-t and Q^k-1, within the Hasse trace range; construct and count E/F_Q with trace t. Compute the exact order of Q modulo r and an explicit pairing witness.
mechanisms.recognition: The embedding degree is the smallest k with Q^k congruent 1 mod r; certify a nondegenerate map on the selected r-subgroup.
mechanisms.witness_requirements: Curve and subgroup identities, exact r and k, auxiliary pairing point, transfer output, and destination field representation.
mechanisms.selected_subgroup_gate: The chosen pairing map must be injective on the target subgroup; compare the destination DLP cost under the same target contract.

mechanisms.name: A j=1728 supersingular construction
mechanisms.construction: For a prime p>3 with p congruent 3 mod 4, choose a nonzero a in F_p and E: y^2=x^3+a*x. Count E, specify a prime-to-p subgroup r, and compute its actual embedding degree and destination field.
mechanisms.recognition: The CM reduction gives supersingularity under the stated congruence; certify nonsingularity and the exact selected subgroup separately.
mechanisms.witness_requirements: Prime p, coefficient a, exact order/trace, selected r and generator, and pairing witness if a transfer claim is made.
mechanisms.selected_subgroup_gate: Supersingularity is a structural property; the subgroup and finite-field DLP cost decide any comparative claim.

mechanisms.name: Cubic norm-one covering over F_(p^6)
mechanisms.construction: Choose p>3, q=p^2, L=F_(q^3). Choose lambda in L^x with lambda^(q^2+q+1)=1 and lambda not 1. Recover nonzero alpha with alpha^q=lambda*alpha (Hilbert 90), require alpha outside F_q, and form E: y^2=x(x-alpha)(x-alpha^q), including the documented twists. Count E, then build and verify the published genus-three cover over F_q and the induced map to Res_(L/F_q)(E).
mechanisms.recognition: The model parameter passes the torus and nonsingularity checks; an ordinary class is screened by the proved v2(f_pi)>=2 condition and then decided by the exact selected CM-order intersection or finite exceptional oracle.
mechanisms.witness_requirements: Exact field and alpha, model hash, point count, smooth genus-three source, cover/map and kernel checks, and independent class/model replay.
mechanisms.selected_subgroup_gate: Give r and G, prove the induced map acts injectively on the selected r-subgroup, and account for construction, transport and destination solver costs.

mechanisms.name: Nonsplit quadratic covering branch over F_(p^6)
mechanisms.construction: Choose p>3, q=p^2, L=F_(q^3) and a base-field nonsquare d. Select an admissible nonidentity parameter in the quadratic torus of order q^2-q+1 in F_(q^6); use the published Cayley reconstruction to obtain alpha and E: y^2=(x^2-d)(x-alpha)(x-alpha^q). Count E and verify the genus-three cover and its map.
mechanisms.recognition: Use the exact invariant/torus test on the model; for ordinary classes use the selected-floor CM intersection and handle exceptional units with the finite oracle.
mechanisms.witness_requirements: The nonsquare and parameter witnesses, exact curve/field representation, point count, smooth cover, map, and independent replay.
mechanisms.selected_subgroup_gate: Specify r and G and verify kernel avoidance and subgroup transport.

mechanisms.name: Published Type I cubic-extension coverings
mechanisms.construction: Enumerate distinct admissible Type I Frobenius-root configurations alpha, alpha^q, beta, beta^q and the paper's leading-coefficient square classes, then construct the genus-three cover and verify the isogeny condition.
mechanisms.recognition: Apply the published Type I quadratic-equation and hyperellipticity tests, with all root exclusions.
mechanisms.witness_requirements: Field of every root, exact curve and covering equations, smoothness/genus, map, and normalized equivalence class.
mechanisms.selected_subgroup_gate: Transfer is a separate map-and-kernel check for the chosen r-subgroup.

mechanisms.name: Published Type II cubic-extension coverings
mechanisms.construction: Enumerate the admissible Type II root configuration alpha, alpha^(q^3), alpha^q, alpha^(q^4) in the stated sixth-degree ambient field, retain the leading-coefficient square class and twists, then construct the genus-three cover and verify the isogeny condition.
mechanisms.recognition: Apply the published Type II conjugate-root and Legendre-normalization tests, including the stated exclusions.
mechanisms.witness_requirements: Root fields, exact curve and covering equations, smoothness/genus, map, square class and normalized equivalence class.
mechanisms.selected_subgroup_gate: Transfer is a separate map-and-kernel check for the chosen r-subgroup.

mechanisms.name: Binary Weil-descent coefficient control
mechanisms.construction: Fix F_(2^(mn))/F_(2^m), enumerate ordinary nonsingular binary elliptic models in a frozen coefficient space, and select coefficients with a prescribed Frobenius span. Construct the GHS cover and verify its actual genus and map.
mechanisms.recognition: Check the coefficient span under Frobenius and the published descent hypotheses on the exact field representation.
mechanisms.witness_requirements: Frozen coefficient law, source curve, cover equation, genus, induced map and exact field conversions.
mechanisms.selected_subgroup_gate: The induced map must preserve and inject the selected subgroup; cost includes field conversion and destination arithmetic.

mechanisms.name: Odd-prime polarized cubic restriction
mechanisms.construction: Choose a cubic extension and a source elliptic curve satisfying the published odd-prime isogeny and polarization hypotheses; construct a maximal isotropic kernel and a principally polarized quotient, then identify and verify its genus-three Jacobian model.
mechanisms.recognition: Verify the kernel is isotropic and rational, the quotient polarization is principal, and the target is a Jacobian with an explicit transport map.
mechanisms.witness_requirements: Source identity, prime degree, kernel generators, polarization certificate, target curve and map.
mechanisms.selected_subgroup_gate: Check prime-to-kernel subgroup transport for the chosen r and charge map construction/evaluation.

mechanisms.name: Transport to a verified covering representative
mechanisms.construction: Within a certified ordinary isogeny class, construct an ordered route to a model with a verified covering and preserve explicit maps, degrees, kernels and field definitions at every edge.
mechanisms.recognition: A matching trace shows class membership; an executable route requires independently checked maps and a compatible selected subgroup.
mechanisms.witness_requirements: Separate source/target curve IDs, ordered edge certificates, transported G and Q, and exact source/target subgroup orders.
mechanisms.selected_subgroup_gate: Every edge must be injective on the chosen subgroup; include route and reverse-log costs in any comparison.

mechanisms.name: Selected points from a proper subfield
mechanisms.construction: Choose E over a proper subfield F_(p^d) of F_(p^n), extend its coefficients, then choose and certify a selected subgroup whose generator and all intended targets are rational over F_(p^d).
mechanisms.recognition: Verify coefficient/model descent, point coordinates and subgroup containment separately; j-invariant descent alone does not certify the point condition.
mechanisms.witness_requirements: Exact subfield embedding, model isomorphism where needed, generator/target coordinates and order.
mechanisms.selected_subgroup_gate: The actual selected points must lie in the smaller group before a smaller-field DLP comparison is relevant.
